howto.name: Choose a PDF
howto.text: Choose the PDF you want to make fillable. Its pages are previewed in your browser. The fields are placed on top of its existing pages, and its bookmarks, links and comments are kept.

howto.name: Detect fields, or place them yourself
howto.text: For a PDF drawn as a form but not fillable (a printed form, a Word form saved as PDF, a government form without fields), click Detect fields. The PDF is uploaded and PrivaTools looks for the blanks it draws: lines after labels, empty boxes and table cells, and checkboxes. It proposes text, date, checkbox and signature fields named after their labels, dashed on the page. Or click Draw a field and drag a box on the page preview, or click Add and type the page, X, Y, width and height in points from the top-left corner. On a page the PDF stores turned, typed values count from the corner that is top left before the turn; the preview shows where each field goes.

howto.name: Review every proposal
howto.text: Accept the proposals that are right, one by one or all at once, change a name or a type first if you like, and reject the rest. Nothing becomes a field until you accept it. An accepted field can be moved, resized and changed like one you drew, and a date becomes a text field. Give each field a name and choose its type: text, checkbox, radio buttons, dropdown, list or signature.

howto.name: Configure form properties
howto.text: Set default values, mark fields as required, allow several lines in a text field, pre-tick checkboxes, and type the options for radio buttons, dropdowns and lists, separated by commas. A radio field gets one button per option inside its box, each labelled with its option; the labels are set in Helvetica, so accented Western European letters print, but other characters, such as the euro sign, curly quotes or Cyrillic, show as dots.

howto.name: Export the fillable PDF
howto.text: Click Generate fillable PDF. The download contains standard AcroForm fields, the interactive form format PDF readers use; test it in the reader your recipients use.

faq.q: How does Detect fields find the fields?
faq.a: It reads what the PDF's pages draw and say, by fixed rules rather than AI: a line drawn, typed as underscores or set as dots after a label ("Name: ____"), a line with a caption under it ("Signature of applicant"), lines stacked under a question, empty and rounded boxes, pale shaded areas, the empty cells of a ruled table, the space under a small caption in a cell, a row of boxes for one character each, and checkbox squares and box characters such as ☐. A label that says date makes a date field, one that says signature or sign here a signature field. Each proposal is named after its nearest label and marked Likely or Possible by how clearly the page draws it; neither is a promise.

faq.q: What can Detect fields miss or get wrong?
faq.a: A scanned form: its pages are pictures, with no drawn lines or boxes to find, and OCR PDF adds text, not lines, so place the fields by hand. It can also miss blanks with no label near them, labels far from their line or written after it (as right-to-left forms, in Arabic or Hebrew, place them), the blank column of a table that is mostly filled in, fields drawn as pictures, and radio buttons and dropdowns (it proposes text, date, checkbox and signature fields only), and it reads at most 50 pages. It can propose a field where there is none, such as a rule under a heading or an empty cell in a table. That is why you review each proposal before anything is created.

faq.q: Is anything added to my form without my review?
faq.a: No. Proposals are drawn dashed on the page and listed apart from the fields you placed. Only the ones you accept become fields, and only those are in the PDF you create. Fields the PDF already has are left alone, and nothing is proposed over them; to fill those in, use Fill Form.

The page preview is drawn in your browser. When you click Detect fields, the PDF is uploaded to PrivaTools, read in temporary storage and deleted after the answer, which holds the proposed fields and the labels they were named after. When you create the form, the PDF and the fields are uploaded again and deleted after that response. Nothing is kept, and nothing goes to an AI provider.

faq.q: What field types can I add?
faq.a: Single-line and multi-line text fields, checkboxes, radio buttons, dropdowns, list boxes, and empty signature fields. There are no date pickers: a date is a text field. There are no comb fields either: a row of boxes for one character each becomes one text field, so what is typed in it is not spaced one character to a box.

faq.q: Will the form work in Adobe Reader?
faq.a: It should. The fields are standard AcroForm fields, the form format that Adobe Reader and other common PDF viewers support, and the file asks viewers to draw the fields' appearance themselves. Open the finished form in the reader your recipients use before sending it.

faq.q: Can I set fields as required?
faq.a: Yes. Tick Required on a field to set the PDF required flag; how it is enforced depends on the PDF reader and on how the form is submitted. Validation rules such as numeric-only or email format are not available.
